title: Amsterdam Open World game
author: TrainingMonk8586
selftext:
Hey everyone!

Just wanted to share a little hobby project I’ve been working on. Well, it started as a hobby project, but two weeks and way too many hours later, I think I might need to stop and move on to the next thing. 😅

It’s called **Mokum Madness**, a GTA-style game set in Amsterdam, built using real OpenStreetMap data.  
You can explore the city, steal a car, grab a bicycle or boat, and drive around Amsterdam. There are also 42 missions, police chases, multiplayer, local radio stations, and a day/night cycle.

I built it using Claude Code and Codex, mostly as an experiment to see how far I could get with AI-assisted development.

The first results genuinely impressed. Within a few hours, I had a playable map of Amsterdam and could drive around the streets. Getting from that initial proof of concept to something polished, smooth, and actually entertaining, though, is a whole different story. That’s where most of the work is!

But even in its current state, I’ve caught myself just driving around, exploring familiar streets and discovering the city in a completely different way.

Anyway, I’m curious what you guys think! It’s definitely not as impressive visually as some of the project I’ve seen here, but still wanted to share 😇

**Here’s the link:** [www.mokum-madness.com](https://mokum-madness.com/)

comments.author: Successful-Fig-7330
comments.body:
The harvesting of OpenStreetMap and the resulting map is cool, but the roads are very rough, I think a lot more effort is needed in how to interpret that data into the desired layouts for the game world. That's the most interesting aspect of this project to me.

The collisions whilst driving, when objects aren't disappearing in front of you, feel satisfying. The interior location i found felt very confused, like just because you can add them doesn't mean the gameplay would benefit.

Generally the physics are pretty wonky and although it appears on the surface to be 90% there, in reality I think that last 10% going to be a lot more effort than everything so far.

Ultimately, though, GTA1 released 30 years ago and all other top down derivatives didn't really add anything. Of course, GTA1 is still a far far superior game to this, with great sound, music, humour, character, etc etc.

I can see value in the idea of a modern GTA1 where AI can bring in maps from real cities, because driving around familiar streets is a nice novelty (and one of the reasons 2002s The Getaway was compelling for Londoners).

replies.author: TrainingMonk8586
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback! And to be clear, I don't think me, using AI to build a game can compete with a refined game like GTA 1, even if that game is 30 years old.   
  
Maybe for me it was also the fun of playing a game in my own neighbourhood. I guess that was also a bit of the essence why I started with this. To make it very local, as there will not be many game developers making a game specifically about your town or city.  

But as you also mentioned, getting something out there thats 90% okay-ish doesn't make it feel good. And that last 10% indeed needs a loooot more effort. 

Again, thanks for the reply. Maybe next I will see if I can do Prince of Persia.. but then the Amsterdam version too :P
